sentences.zh: 初，孝成事唐獻祖為愛將，獻祖之失振武，為吐渾所攻，部下離散，孝成獨奮忠義，解蔚州之圍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiaocheng served Tang's Xianzu as a favored general; when Xianzu lost Zhenwu and was attacked by the Tuyuhun, his followers scattered, yet Xiaocheng alone exerted loyal righteousness and lifted the siege of Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiaocheng had been a favorite of Xianzu; when Xianzu lost Zhenwu to Tuyuhun attack and his men scattered, Xiaocheng alone held loyal and broke the siege of Wei.

sentences.zh: 武皇之鎮雁門也，孝成厭代，帝年甫十三，善騎射，獻祖見而撫之曰：「英氣如父，可侍吾左右。

translations.literal: When Wuhuang held Yanmen, Xiaocheng was in Dai, and the Emperor was just thirteen, skilled at mounted archery; Xianzu saw him, stroked him, and said, "Spirit like your father—you may attend at my side.
translations.idiomatic: While Wuhuang held Yanmen, thirteen-year-old Siyuan, then in Dai, impressed Xianzu with his riding and archery; Xianzu stroked him and said, "Spirit like your father—you may wait on me.

sentences.zh: 」每從圍獵，仰射飛鳥，控弦必中，尋隸武皇帳下。

translations.literal: " On every hunt he shot upward at flying birds and never missed the string; soon he was attached to Wuhuang's command tent.
translations.idiomatic: " On hunts he shot birds on the wing without a miss and soon joined Wuhuang's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 武皇遇上源之難，將佐罹害者甚眾，帝時年十七，翼武皇逾垣脫難，於亂兵流矢之內，獨無所傷。

translations.literal: When Wuhuang met disaster at Shangyuan, very many aides suffered harm; the Emperor was then seventeen, aided Wuhuang over the wall to escape, and amid mutinous troops and flying arrows was alone unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangyuan, when many of Wuhuang's officers were killed, seventeen-year-old Siyuan helped him over the wall to safety and came through the mutiny and arrows unscathed.

sentences.zh: 武皇鎮河東，以帝掌親騎。

translations.literal: When Wuhuang held Hedong, he put the Emperor in charge of his personal cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuhuang held Hedong he made Siyuan commander of his bodyguard horse.

sentences.zh: 時李存信為蕃漢大將，每總兵征討，師多不利，武皇遂選帝副之，所向克捷。

translations.literal: At the time Li Cunxin was overall Han and non-Han general; whenever he led troops on campaign the army mostly fared ill, so Wuhuang chose the Emperor as his deputy, and wherever he went he won.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin, Han and non-Han overall commander, often lost on campaign; Wuhuang paired Siyuan with him and thereafter the columns won.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗宿於雁門逆旅，媼方娠，不時具饌，媼聞腹中兒語云：「大家至矣，速宜進食。

translations.literal: The Emperor once lodged at a Yanmen inn; an old woman was pregnant and had not timely prepared food when the woman heard a voice from her belly say, "The great lord has come—hurry and serve food.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan once stayed at a Yanmen inn; a pregnant landlady had not yet cooked when her unborn child said, "The great lord is here—serve food at once.

sentences.zh: 」媼異之，遽起，親奉庖爨甚恭；

translations.literal: " The woman marveled, rose at once, and personally tended the kitchen with great respect;
translations.idiomatic: " Startled, she rose and waited on him in the kitchen with great respect;

sentences.zh: 帝詰之，媼告其故。

translations.literal: the Emperor questioned her, and the woman told the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan asked why, and she told him.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》云：帝以媼前倨後恭，詰之，曰：「公貴不可言也。

translations.literal: (The 《Beimeng Suoyan》 says: because the woman had been arrogant before and respectful after, the Emperor questioned her; she said, "Your nobility cannot be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Beimeng Suoyan》 says Siyuan asked why the landlady had been rude then deferential; she said, "Your rank is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」問其故，具道娠子腹語事，帝曰：「老媼遜言，懼吾辱耳。

translations.literal: " Asked the reason, she fully told of the pregnant child's belly speech; the Emperor said, "The old woman flatters—she fears to shame me.
translations.idiomatic: " She told the belly-speech story; Siyuan said, "She flatters—she fears to shame me.

sentences.zh: 」後果如其言。）〉

translations.literal: " Later it indeed proved as she had said.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Later events proved her right.)〉

sentences.zh: 帝既壯，雄武獨斷，謙和下士。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had grown strong, he was martial and decisive alone, yet humble and gentle toward officers.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, Siyuan was fierce and self-reliant yet humble with his officers.

sentences.zh: 每有戰功，未嘗自伐。

translations.literal: Whenever he had battle merit, he never boasted of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He never boasted of his victories.

sentences.zh: 居常惟治兵仗，持廉處靜，晏如也。

translations.literal: In daily life he only trained weapons and gear, held to integrity in quiet, and was perfectly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he drilled arms, lived plainly and quietly, and was perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 武皇常試之，召於泉府，命恣其所取，帝惟持束帛數緡而出。

translations.literal: Wuhuang often tested him, summoning him to the treasury office and ordering him to take whatever he wished; the Emperor took only several bolts of silk and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang tested him at the treasury and told him to take what he liked; Siyuan took only a few bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 凡所賜與，分給部下。

translations.literal: Whatever he was given, he divided among his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he received he shared with his men.

sentences.zh: 常與諸將會，諸將矜衒武勇，帝徐曰：「公輩以口擊賊，吾以手擊賊。

translations.literal: He often met with the generals; when the generals vaunted their martial valor, the Emperor said slowly, "You gentlemen strike the enemy with your mouths—I strike the enemy with my hands.
translations.idiomatic: At councils when generals vaunted their prowess, Siyuan said, "You strike the enemy with your mouths—I strike with my hands.

sentences.zh: 」眾慚而止。

translations.literal: " The crowd in shame fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: " The others fell silent in shame.

sentences.zh: 景福初，黑山戍將王弁據振武叛，帝率其屬攻之，擒弁以獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingfu, Black Mountain garrison commander Wang Bian seized Zhenwu in rebellion; the Emperor led his followers to attack, captured Bian, and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingfu 1 Wang Bian of the Black Mountain garrison rebelled at Zhenwu; Siyuan attacked, captured him, and presented him to Wuhuang.

sentences.zh: 乾寧三年，梁人急攻兗、鄆，鄆帥朱瑄求救於武皇。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianning, Liang forces pressed Yan and Yun fiercely; Yan military commissioner Zhu Xuan begged Wuhuang for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 3 Liang armies pressed Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan of Yan begged Wuhuang for aid.

sentences.zh: 武皇先遣騎將李承嗣、史儼援之，復遣李存信將兵三萬屯於莘縣。

translations.literal: Wuhuang first sent cavalry generals Li Chengsi and Shi Yan to aid them, then again sent Li Cunxin with thirty thousand troops to camp at Shen county.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang first sent Li Chengsi and Shi Yan with horse, then Li Cunxin with thirty thousand men to Shen.

sentences.zh: 聞汴軍益盛，攻兗甚急，存信遣帝率三百騎而往，敗汴軍於任城，遂解兗州之圍。

translations.literal: Hearing Bian armies growing stronger and the Yan assault very urgent, Cunxin sent the Emperor with three hundred horse; he defeated Bian troops at Rencheng and thus lifted the siege of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: As Bian pressure mounted on Yan, Cunxin sent Siyuan with three hundred horse; he routed Bian forces at Rencheng and lifted the siege of Yan.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾見帝，執手涕謝。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin saw the Emperor, took his hand, and wept thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin took Siyuan's hand and wept his thanks.

sentences.zh: 其年，魏帥羅宏信背盟，襲破李存信於莘縣，帝奮命殿軍而還，武皇嘉其功，即以所屬五百騎號曰「橫衝都」；

translations.literal: That year Wei military commissioner Luo Hongxin broke alliance and smashed Li Cunxin at Shen county; the Emperor fought desperately to cover the rear retreat, and Wuhuang praised his merit, at once naming his five hundred horse "Hengchong Command";
translations.idiomatic: That year Luo Hongxin of Wei broke faith and routed Li Cunxin at Shen; Siyuan fought a desperate rearguard, and Wuhuang rewarded him by naming his five hundred horse the Hengchong Command;

sentences.zh: 侍於帳下，故兩河間目帝為李橫衝。

translations.literal: he attended at the command tent, so between the two He provinces people called the Emperor Li Hengchong.
translations.idiomatic: they served in Wuhuang's tent, and between the two He provinces men called him Li Hengchong.

sentences.zh: 明年，武皇遣大將軍李嗣昭率師下馬嶺關，將復邢、洺，梁將葛從周以兵應援。

translations.literal: The next year Wuhuang sent great general Li Sizhao to lead troops down through Maling Pass to recover Xing and Ming; Liang general Ge Congzhou came with troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao through Maling Pass to recover Xing and Ming; Ge Congzhou of Liang marched to meet him.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭兵敗，退入青山口，梁軍扼其路，步兵不戰自潰，嗣昭不能制。

translations.literal: Sizhao's army was defeated and withdrew into Qingshan Pass; Liang troops blocked the road, infantry scattered without fighting, and Sizhao could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao was beaten back into Qingshan Pass; Liang blocked the road, foot soldiers scattered without a fight, and Sizhao could not hold them.

sentences.zh: 會帝本軍至，謂嗣昭曰：「步兵雖散，若吾輩空回，大事去矣。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's own army arrived, he said to Sizhao, "Though the foot soldiers are scattered, if we return empty-handed the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Siyuan's column arrived he told Sizhao, "Though the foot have scattered, an empty retreat loses everything.

sentences.zh: 為公試決一戰，不捷而死，差勝被囚。

translations.literal: For you I will try one decisive battle—if we do not win, death is still better than capture.
translations.idiomatic: Let me try one fight for you—if we fail, death beats chains.

sentences.zh: 」嗣昭曰：「吾為卿副。

translations.literal: " Sizhao said, "I will be your deputy.
translations.idiomatic: " Sizhao said, "I follow you.

sentences.zh: 」帝率其屬，解鞍礪鏃，憑高列陣，左右指畫，梁人莫之測，因呼曰：「吾王命我取葛司徒，他士可無並命。

translations.literal: " The Emperor led his followers, unslung saddles and sharpened arrowheads, drew up on high ground and pointed left and right; Liang men could not gauge him, so he shouted, "Our king has ordered me to take Minister Ge—other men need not die with him.
translations.idiomatic: " Siyuan's men unslung, sharpened arrows, and formed on the heights; Liang troops could not read him, and he shouted, "Our king sent me for Minister Ge—let the rest stand aside.

sentences.zh: 」即徑犯其陣，奮擊如神。

translations.literal: " He at once charged their formation, striking like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: " He charged straight in, fighting like a god.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭繼進，梁軍即時退去，帝與嗣昭收兵入關。

translations.literal: Sizhao followed in, Liang armies at once withdrew, and the Emperor and Sizhao gathered troops back through the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao pressed after; Liang withdrew, and Siyuan and Sizhao brought the army back through the pass.

sentences.zh: 帝四中流矢，血流被股，武皇解衣授藥，手賜卮酒，撫其背曰：「吾兒神人也！

translations.literal: The Emperor was struck by four stray arrows, blood soaking his thigh; Wuhuang removed his robe to apply medicine, personally gave a cup of wine, and stroked his back, saying, "My son is a spirit!
translations.idiomatic: Four stray arrows struck Siyuan and blood soaked his thigh; Wuhuang stripped his own robe to dress the wounds, handed him wine, and stroked his back: "My son is a god!

sentences.zh: 微吾兒，幾為從周所笑。

translations.literal: But for my son, we would nearly have been laughed at by Congzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Without you, Congzhou would have had the laugh on us.

sentences.zh: 」自青山之戰，名聞天下。

translations.literal: " From the Qingshan battle his name was heard throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " After Qingshan his fame spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 天復中，梁祖遣氏叔琮將兵五萬，營於洞渦。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era Liang Founder sent Shi Shuzong with fifty thousand troops to camp at Donghuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu years Liang's founder sent Shi Shuzong with fifty thousand men to camp at Donghuo.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸道之師畢萃於太原，郡縣多陷於梁，晉陽城外，營壘相望。

translations.literal: At the time armies of every circuit had all gathered at Taiyuan; many prefectures and counties had fallen to Liang, and outside Jinyang city camps faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit had troops at Taiyuan; many counties had fallen to Liang, and camps ringed Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 武皇登陴號令，不遑飲食。

translations.literal: Wuhuang mounted the ramparts to shout orders and had no leisure to eat or drink.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang walked the walls shouting orders and scarcely ate or drank.

sentences.zh: 屬大雨彌旬，城壘多壞，武皇令帝與李嗣昭分兵四出，突入諸營，梁軍由是引退；

translations.literal: As great rain lasted more than ten days and many ramparts and walls were ruined, Wuhuang ordered the Emperor and Li Sizhao to divide troops four ways, burst into the various camps, and Liang armies thereby withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: After ten days of rain wrecked the walls, Wuhuang sent Siyuan and Li Sizhao in four columns to storm Liang camps and drive them off;

sentences.zh: 帝率偏師追襲，復諸郡邑。

translations.literal: the Emperor led a detached force in pursuit and recovered the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan pursued with a detached force and recovered the lost counties.

sentences.zh: 昭宗之幸鳳翔也，梁祖率眾攻圍岐下，武皇奉詔應援，遣李嗣昭、周德威出師晉、絳，營於蒲縣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong went to Fengxiang, Liang Founder led the masses to besiege Qi below; Wuhuang received the edict to aid and sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei to march from Jin and Jiang, camping at Pu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong fled to Fengxiang, Liang besieged Qi; Wuhuang marched to aid and sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei from Jin and Jiang to camp at Pu.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭等軍，大為梁將朱友寧、氏叔琮所敗，梁之追兵直抵晉陽，營於晉祠，日以步騎環城。

translations.literal: Sizhao and the rest were greatly defeated by Liang generals Zhu Youning and Shi Shuzong; Liang pursuers pressed straight to Jinyang and camped at Jinci, daily circling the city with foot and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youning and Shi Shuzong crushed Sizhao at Pu; Liang pursuers reached Jinyang, camped at Jinci, and ringed the city daily with foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 武皇登城督眾，憂形於色。

translations.literal: Wuhuang mounted the city to oversee the masses, worry showing on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang walked the walls to rally the troops, worry plain on his face.

sentences.zh: 攻城既急，武皇與大將謀，欲出奔雲中。

translations.literal: As the assault grew urgent, Wuhuang consulted great generals and wished to flee to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: With the assault tightening, Wuhuang and his generals planned flight to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「攻守之謀，據城百倍，但兒等在，必能固守。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "For attack and defense, holding the city is a hundredfold better—only while we sons are here we can surely hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan said, "Defense from the walls beats any other plan a hundred times over—as long as we are here, the city will hold.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuhuang stayed.

sentences.zh: 居數日，潰軍稍集，率敢死之士，日夜分出諸門掩襲梁軍，擒其驍將遊昆侖等。

translations.literal: After several days scattered troops gradually gathered; he led dare-to-die men day and night out through the gates in raids on Liang armies and captured their fierce generals You Kunlun and others.
translations.idiomatic: Within days scattered men rallied; Siyuan led dare-to-die troops out by night through every gate, raided Liang camps, and seized fierce generals including You Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 梁軍失勢，乃燒營而退。

translations.literal: Liang armies lost momentum and burned their camps and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liang lost heart, burned their camps, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天祐五年五月，莊宗親將兵以救潞州之圍，帝時領突騎左右軍與周德威分為二廣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Tianyou 5 Zhuangzong personally led troops to rescue the siege of Luzhou; the Emperor then commanded the assault cavalry left and right armies with Zhou Dewei as two wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianyou 5 Zhuangzong marched in person to break the siege of Luzhou; Siyuan led the assault horse of the left and right guards with Zhou Dewei on the flanks.

sentences.zh: 帝晨至夾城東北隅，命斧其鹿角，負芻填塹，下馬乘城大噪。

translations.literal: At dawn the Emperor reached the northeast corner of Jiacheng, ordered the palisade stakes hewn, carried fodder to fill the moat, dismounted, scaled the wall, and shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Siyuan reached Jiacheng's northeast corner, had stakes cut, fodder thrown into the ditch, climbed the wall on foot, and roared.

sentences.zh: 時德威登西北隅，亦噪以應之。

translations.literal: At the time Dewei mounted the northwest corner and also shouted in answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei on the northwest corner answered with a roar of his own.

sentences.zh: 帝先入夾城，大破梁軍，是日解圍，其功居最。

translations.literal: The Emperor entered Jiacheng first, greatly smashed Liang armies, and that day the siege was lifted—his merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan broke into Jiacheng first, routed Liang, and won first credit when the siege lifted that day.

sentences.zh: 柏鄉之役，兩軍既成列，莊宗以梁軍甚盛，慮師入之怯，欲激壯之，手持白金巨鍾賜帝酒，謂之曰：「卿見南軍白馬、赤馬都否？

translations.literal: At the battle of Baixiang, when both armies had formed ranks, Zhuangzong, because Liang armies were very strong, feared his troops would enter battle timid and wished to stir their courage, personally held a great white-gold goblet to bestow wine on the Emperor, and said to him, "Do you see the Liang army's White Horse and Red Horse Commands?
translations.idiomatic: At Baixiang, with both armies drawn up, Zhuangzong feared his men would falter before strong Liang lines and personally raised a great white-gold cup to toast Siyuan: "Do you see Liang's White Horse and Red Horse Commands?

sentences.zh: 睹之令人膽破。

translations.literal: To look on them makes one's gall break.
translations.idiomatic: The sight alone breaks the heart.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「彼虛有其表耳，翌日當歸吾廄中。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "They are empty show—tomorrow they will be in our stables.
translations.idiomatic: " Siyuan said, "They are show—tomorrow they belong in our stables.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗拊髀大笑曰：「卿已氣吞之矣！

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong slapped his thigh and laughed greatly, saying, "You have already swallowed them in spirit!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong slapped his thigh and laughed: "You have already swallowed them whole!

sentences.zh: 」帝引鍾盡酹，即屬揮弭，躍馬挺身，與其部下百人直犯白馬都，奮楇舞槊，生挾二騎校而回，飛矢麗帝甲如蝟毛焉。

translations.literal: " The Emperor took the goblet, drained it in libation, then took his bow, leaped his horse and thrust out his body, and with his hundred followers charged straight at the White Horse Command, brandishing clubs and whirling spears, seized two cavalry officers alive and returned; flying arrows studded the Emperor's armor like hedgehog quills.
translations.idiomatic: " Siyuan drained the cup, seized his bow, and with a hundred men charged the White Horse Command, club and spear swinging, seized two officers alive, and rode back with his armor bristling with arrows.

sentences.zh: 由是三軍增氣，自辰及未，騎軍百戰，帝往來衝擊，執訊獲醜，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Thereby the three armies gained spirit; from the hour chen to wei the cavalry fought a hundred clashes, the Emperor charging back and forth, taking captives and severed ears beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Morale surged; from midmorning to midafternoon the horse fought a hundred rounds while Siyuan charged back and forth, taking prisoners and heads beyond count.

sentences.zh: 是日，梁軍大敗，以功授代州刺史。

translations.literal: That day Liang armies were greatly defeated, and for merit he was made Dai prefectural governor.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was routed that day, and Siyuan was made governor of Dai for his merit.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遣周德威伐幽州，帝分兵略定山後八軍，與劉守光愛將元行欽戰於廣邊軍，凡八戰，帝控弦發矢七中。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong sent Zhou Dewei to attack Youzhou; the Emperor divided troops to pacify the eight armies behind the mountains and fought Liu Shouguang's favorite Yuan Xingqin at Guangbian Army in eight battles—the Emperor drew the bow and seven of seven arrows struck home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong sent Zhou Dewei against Youzhou, Siyuan pacified the eight rear-mountain commands and fought Yuan Xingqin, Liu Shouguang's favorite, at Guangbian in eight clashes, landing seven of seven shots.

sentences.zh: 行欽酣戰不解，矢亦中帝股，拔矢復戰。

translations.literal: Xingqin fought fiercely without respite; an arrow also struck the Emperor's thigh—he pulled the arrow and fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin fought on without pause; an arrow struck Siyuan's thigh—he pulled it and kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 行欽窮蹙，面縛乞降，帝酌酒飲之，拊其背曰：「吾子，壯士也！

translations.literal: Xingqin was cornered, bound his face, and begged surrender; the Emperor poured wine for him to drink, patted his back, and said, "My boy, what a brave fellow!
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Xingqin bound his face and surrendered; Siyuan gave him wine, clapped his back, and said, "My boy, what a fighter!

sentences.zh: 」因厚遇之。

translations.literal: " He therefore treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: " He treated him generously thereafter.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，莊宗與梁將劉鄩大戰於故元城北，帝以三千騎環之，鼓噪奮擊，內外合勢，鄩軍殆盡。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year Zhuangzong fought a great battle with Liang general Liu Yan north of old Yuan city; the Emperor with three thousand horse encircled them, drumming and shouting in fierce attack, inner and outer combining force, and Yan's army was nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 13 Zhuangzong fought Liu Yan of Liang north of old Yuan city; Siyuan ringed him with three thousand horse, drumming and charging in concert until Yan's army was nearly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 帝徇地慈、洺。

translations.literal: The Emperor pacified ground in Ci and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan pacified Ci and Ming.

sentences.zh: 四月，相州張筠遁走，乃以帝為相州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Xiangzhou's Zhang Yun fled; he was then made Xiang prefectural governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhang Yun fled Xiangzhou, and Siyuan was made governor of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 九月，滄州節度使戴思遠棄城歸汴，小將毛璋據州納款，莊宗命率兵慰撫。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Cangzhou military commissioner Dai Siyuan abandoned the city and returned to Bian; junior officer Mao Zhang held the prefecture and submitted allegiance, and Zhuangzong ordered the Emperor to lead troops to comfort and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Dai Siyuan of Cangzhou abandoned his post for Bian; Mao Zhang seized the city and submitted; Zhuangzong sent Siyuan to reassure it.

sentences.zh: 既入城，以軍府乂安報莊宗，書吏誤云：「已至滄州，禮上畢。

translations.literal: After entering the city he reported Zhuangzong that the military government was settled; a clerk mistakenly wrote, "Already reached Cangzhou—the rites of submission are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city he reported the garrison secure, but a clerk wrote by mistake, "Reached Cangzhou—submission rites complete.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗省狀，怒曰：「嗣源反耶！

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong read the report and raged, saying, "Has Siyuan rebelled!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong read it and raged: "Has Siyuan rebelled?

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之懼，歸罪於書吏，斬之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, hearing, was afraid, blamed the clerk, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " Alarmed, Siyuan blamed the clerk and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 未幾，承製授邢州節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he received appointment by imperial rescript as Xingzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an imperial rescript made him military commissioner of Xing.

sentences.zh: 十四年四月，契丹安巴堅率眾攻幽州，周德威間使告急，莊宗召諸將議進取之計，諸將咸言：「敵勢不能持久，野無所掠，食盡自還，然後踵而擊之可也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year Khitan Anbajian led the masses to attack Youzhou; Zhou Dewei sent messengers between to report urgency, and Zhuangzong summoned generals to discuss plans to advance and take them; the generals all said, "The enemy's force cannot last long—with nothing to plunder in the wild, when food is gone they will return of themselves, and then we may follow and strike.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 14 Khitan Anbajian besieged Youzhou; Zhou Dewei sent urgent word, and Zhuangzong asked his generals how to relieve it; they said the Khitan could not stay long and should be struck only after they withdrew for hunger.

sentences.zh: 」帝奏曰：「德威盡忠於家國，孤城被攻，危亡在即，不宜更待敵衰。

translations.literal: " The Emperor memorialized, saying, "Dewei is wholly loyal to the state and clan; a lone city under attack, peril and ruin are imminent—it is not fitting to wait further for the enemy to weaken.
translations.idiomatic: " Siyuan replied, "Dewei is wholly loyal; his lone city faces ruin—we must not wait for the Khitan to weaken.

sentences.zh: 願假臣突騎五千為前鋒以援之。

translations.literal: I ask to be lent five thousand assault horse as vanguard to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Lend me five thousand assault horse as vanguard to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「公言是也。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong said, "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 」即命帝與李存審、閻寶率軍赴援，帝為前鋒，會軍於易州。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered the Emperor with Li Cunshen and Yan Bao to lead armies to the rescue; the Emperor was vanguard and joined armies at Yi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Siyuan with Li Cunshen and Yan Bao; Siyuan led the van and joined the column at Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「敵騎以馬上為生，不須營壘，況彼眾我寡，所宜銜枚箝馬，潛行溪澗，襲其不備也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the generals, "Enemy horse live on the saddle and need no camps; moreover they are many and we few—we should hold arrows in the mouth, clamp the horses' mouths, steal along streams and ravines, and strike them unprepared."
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan told the generals, "Khitan horse live in the saddle and need no camp; we are few—they are many—so we should march silent along streams and ravines and hit them unawares."

sentences.zh: 八月，師發上穀，陰晦而雨，帝仰天祈祝，即時晴霽，師循大房嶺，緣潤而進。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the army set out from Shanggu; the sky was dim and rainy, the Emperor prayed heavenward, and at once the sky cleared; the army followed Dafang Ridge and advanced along the moist ravines.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the column left Shanggu in rain; Siyuan prayed, the sky cleared, and they marched Dafang Ridge along hidden ravines.

sentences.zh: 翌日，敵騎大至，每遇穀口，敵騎扼其前，帝與長子從珂奮命血戰，敵即解去，我軍方得前進。

translations.literal: The next day enemy horse came in great numbers; whenever they met a valley mouth enemy horse blocked ahead, the Emperor and his eldest son Congke fought desperately in blood, the enemy then released, and our army could advance.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Khitan horse swarmed every pass; Siyuan and his eldest son Congke fought through in blood until the enemy gave way and the column could move on.

sentences.zh: 距幽州兩舍，敵騎復當穀口而陣，我軍失色。

translations.literal: Two stages from Youzhou enemy horse again blocked the valley mouth in formation, and our army turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Two marches from Youzhou the Khitan again blocked the pass, and the army lost color.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為將者受命忘家，臨敵忘身，以身徇國，正在今日。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "For a general, receiving orders he forgets family; facing the enemy he forgets body; giving body for the state—today is the day.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan said, "A general forgets family when he takes command, forgets self when he meets the enemy—today we give our bodies for the state.

sentences.zh: 諸君觀吾父子與敵周旋！

translations.literal: Gentlemen, watch us father and son grapple with the foe!
translations.idiomatic: Watch us father and son take them on!

sentences.zh: 」因挺身入於敵陣，以北語諭之曰：「爾輩非吾敵，吾當與天皇較力耳。

translations.literal: " He then thrust his body into the enemy formation and addressed them in northern speech, saying, "You are no match for us—I will measure strength with the Heavenly Emperor alone.
translations.idiomatic: " He charged the enemy line and shouted in Khitan, "You are not our match—I will measure strength with the Heavenly Emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 」舞槌奮擊，萬眾披靡，俄挾其酋帥而還。

translations.literal: " Brandishing his club he struck fiercely, ten thousand men scattered, and soon he seized their chieftain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Club swinging, he broke ten thousand men, seized their chieftain, and rode back.

sentences.zh: 我軍呼躍奮擊，敵眾大敗，勢如席卷，委棄鎧仗羊馬殆不勝紀。

translations.literal: Our army shouted, leaped, and struck fiercely; the enemy masses were greatly defeated, momentum like a sweeping mat, casting off armor, sheep, and horses almost beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The army roared and charged; the Khitan broke and fled, leaving armor, sheep, and horses beyond count.

sentences.zh: 是日，解圍，大軍入幽州，周德威迎帝，執手歔欷。

translations.literal: That day the siege was lifted; the great army entered Youzhou, and Zhou Dewei met the Emperor, took his hand, and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: That day the siege lifted; the main force entered Youzhou, and Zhou Dewei took Siyuan's hand and wept.

sentences.zh: 九月，班師於魏州，莊宗親出郊勞，進位檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army returned to camp at Weizhou; Zhuangzong personally came out to the suburbs to reward them, and he was advanced to Grand Guardian by inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army camped at Wei; Zhuangzong met them outside the city and advanced Siyuan to Grand Guardian by inspection.

sentences.zh: 十八年十月，從莊宗大破梁將戴思遠於戚城，斬首二萬級。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year he followed Zhuangzong in greatly defeating Liang general Dai Siyuan at Qi city, beheading twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 18 he followed Zhuangzong in routing Dai Siyuan of Liang at Qi city with twenty thousand heads taken.

sentences.zh: 莊宗以帝為蕃漢副總管，加同平章事。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong made the Emperor Han and non-Han deputy overall commander and added Tongping Zhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong made Siyuan Han and non-Han deputy overall commander and added Tongping Zhangshi.

sentences.zh: 二十年，代李存審為滄州節度使。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he replaced Li Cunshen as Cangzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he replaced Li Cunshen as military commissioner of Cang.

sentences.zh: 四月，莊宗即位於鄴宮，帝進位檢校太傅、兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Zhuangzong took the throne at the Ye palace; the Emperor was advanced to Grand Preceptor by inspection and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhuangzong took the throne at Ye; Siyuan was advanced to Grand Preceptor by inspection and made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋命帝率步騎五千襲鄆州，下之，授天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon Zhuangzong ordered the Emperor to lead five thousand foot and horse in a surprise raid on Yun prefecture, took it, and appointed him Tianping military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhuangzong sent Siyuan with five thousand foot and horse to seize Yun by surprise and made him Tianping military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五月，梁人陷德勝南城，圍楊劉，以扼出師之路。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Liang men took the southern city of Desheng and besieged Yangliu, choking the route of advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Liang took Desheng's south city and besieged Yangliu, blocking the line of march.

sentences.zh: 帝孤守汶陽，四面拒寇，久之，莊宗方解楊劉之圍。

translations.literal: The Emperor held Wenyang alone on four sides against raiders; after a long time Zhuangzong finally lifted the Yangliu siege.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan held Wenyang alone against raids on every side until Zhuangzong at last broke the siege of Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 九月，梁將王彥章以步騎萬人迫鄆州，自中都渡汶。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Liang general Wang Yanzhang with ten thousand foot and horse pressed Yun prefecture, crossing the Wen from Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Yanzhang of Liang pressed Yun with ten thousand foot and horse, crossing the Wen from Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 帝遣長子從珂率騎逆戰於遞坊鎮，獲梁將任釗等三百人，彥章退保中都。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent his eldest son Congke to lead horse to meet them in battle at Difang town, captured Liang generals Ren Zhao and three hundred others, and Yanzhang withdrew to hold Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan sent Congke with horse to meet them at Difang, took Ren Zhao and three hundred others, and Yanzhang fell back to Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞其捷，自楊劉引軍至鄆，以帝為前鋒，大破梁軍於中都，生擒王彥章等。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong heard of the victory, led the army from Yangliu to Yun, made the Emperor vanguard, and greatly defeated Liang armies at Zhongdu, capturing Wang Yanzhang and others alive.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the victory, Zhuangzong marched from Yangliu to Yun, put Siyuan in the van, routed Liang at Zhongdu, and took Wang Yanzhang alive.

sentences.zh: 是日，諸將稱賀，莊宗以酒屬帝曰：「昨朕在朝城，諸君多勸朕棄鄆州，以河為界，賴副總管禦侮於前，崇韜畫謀於內，若信李紹宏輩，大事已掃地矣。

translations.literal: That day the generals offered congratulations; Zhuangzong passed wine to the Emperor, saying, "Yesterday I was at Chaocheng; many of you urged me to abandon Yanzhou and take the river as boundary; relying on the deputy overall commander to repel insult in front and Chongtao to scheme within, if I had believed Li Shaohong and his sort, the great affair would already have been swept away.
translations.idiomatic: That day the generals congratulated him; Cunxu handed wine to Siyuan and said, "Yesterday at Chaocheng many of you wanted to abandon Yan and make the river the border; only the deputy overall commander held the front and Chongtao schemed within—had I listened to Li Shaohong and his crowd, the cause would be dust.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗與諸將議兵所向，諸將多云：「青、齊、徐、兗皆空城耳，王師一臨，不戰自下。

translations.literal: 」Zhuangzong and the generals debated where the army should go; many said, "Qing, Qi, Xu, and Yan are all empty cities; once the royal army arrives they will submit without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: 」Cunxu and his generals debated the next target; most said Qing, Qi, Xu, and Yan were empty and would fall without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」惟帝勸莊宗徑取汴州，語在《莊宗紀》中，莊宗嘉之。

translations.literal: 」Only the Emperor urged Zhuangzong to strike Bianzhou directly—the account is in the 《Zhuangzong Annals》—and Zhuangzong was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: 」Only Siyuan urged a direct strike on Bian—the account is in the 《Zhuangzong Annals》—and Cunxu was pleased.

sentences.zh: 帝即時前進，莊宗繼發中都。

translations.literal: The Emperor advanced at once; Zhuangzong followed in launching from Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan marched at once; Cunxu set out from Zhongdu after him.

sentences.zh: 十月己卯，遲明，帝先至汴州，攻封丘門，汴將王瓚開門迎降。

translations.literal: Tenth month, jimao: toward dawn the Emperor reached Bianzhou first, attacked Fengqiu Gate, and Bian general Wang Zan opened the gate to receive and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the tenth month, before dawn, Siyuan reached Bian first, struck Fengqiu Gate, and Wang Zan opened the gate to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝至建國門，聞梁主已殂，乃號令安撫，回軍於封禪寺。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached Jianguo Gate; hearing the Liang ruler had died, he then ordered reassurance and withdrew the army to Fengchan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianguo Gate he learned the Liang ruler was dead, issued orders to calm the city, and withdrew to Fengchan Temple.

sentences.zh: 辰時，莊宗至，帝迎謁路側。

translations.literal: At the chen hour Zhuangzong arrived; the Emperor met and bowed at the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: At chen hour Cunxu arrived; Siyuan met him and bowed by the road.

sentences.zh: 莊宗大悅，手引帝衣，以首觸帝曰：「吾有天下，由公之血戰也，當與公共之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was greatly pleased, took the Emperor's garment in hand, and knocked his head against the Emperor, saying, "I have the realm through your bloody battles—we shall share it.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu was overjoyed, took Siyuan's robe, and pressed his head to him, saying, "I have the realm through your blood—we shall share it.

sentences.zh: 」尋進位兼中書令。

translations.literal: 」Soon he was promoted to concurrent Secretariat director.
translations.idiomatic: 」Soon he was made concurrent Secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 同興二年正月，契丹犯塞，帝受命北征。

translations.literal: Tongxing year 2, first month: the Khitan raided the frontier; the Emperor received orders for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tongxing 2 the Khitan raided the frontier and Siyuan was ordered north.

sentences.zh: 二月，莊宗以郊天禮畢，賜帝鐵券。

translations.literal: Second month: Zhuangzong, the suburban rites being complete, bestowed on the Emperor an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, after the suburban rites, Cunxu granted Siyuan an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 四月，潞州小將楊立叛，帝受詔討之。

translations.literal: Fourth month: Yang Li, a junior officer of Luzhou, rebelled; the Emperor received an edict to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Luzhou junior officer Yang Li rebelled and Siyuan was ordered to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 五月，擒楊立以獻。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Yang Li was captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yang Li was captured and presented.

sentences.zh: 六月，進位太尉，移鎮汴州，代李存審為蕃漢總管。

translations.literal: Sixth month: he was promoted to Grand Preceptor, transferred to hold Bianzhou, replacing Li Cun'an as Han and non-Han overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he became Grand Preceptor, took Bian as military commissioner, and replaced Li Cun'an as Han and non-Han overall commander.

sentences.zh: 十二月，契丹入寇。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: the Khitan entered in raid.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Khitan raided again.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，帝領兵破契丹於涿州，移授鎮州節度使。

translations.literal: Third year, first month: the Emperor led troops and defeated the Khitan at Zhuozhou and was transferred to appoint Zhenzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year three Siyuan defeated the Khitan at Zhuo and was transferred to Zhenzhou as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝領兵過鄴，鄴庫素有禦甲，帝取五百聯以行。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor led troops past Ye, Ye's storehouse had armor for defense; the Emperor took five hundred suits in succession and marched.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, marching past Ye, he took five hundred suits of armor from the Ye storehouse and went on.

sentences.zh: 是歲，莊宗幸鄴，知之，怒甚。

translations.literal: That year Zhuangzong visited Ye, learned of it, and was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cunxu visited Ye, learned of it, and was furious.

sentences.zh: 無何，帝奏請以長子從珂為北京內衙都指揮使，莊宗愈不悅，曰：「軍政在吾，安得為子奏請！

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor memorialized asking that his eldest son Congke be Beijing inner-palace overall commander; Zhuangzong was ever more displeased and said, "Military affairs are mine—how can you memorialize for a son!
translations.idiomatic: Soon Siyuan asked that his eldest son Congke be Beijing inner-palace commander; Cunxu grew angrier and said, "Military affairs are mine—how dare you ask for your son!

sentences.zh: 吾之細鎧，不奉詔旨強取，其意何也？

translations.literal: My fine armor you took by force without edict—what is the meaning of this?
translations.idiomatic: You seized my fine armor without an edict—what did you mean by that?

sentences.zh: 」令留守張憲自往取之，左右說諭，乃止。

translations.literal: 」He ordered regent Zhang Xian to go himself to take it; left and right urged and explained, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 」He ordered regent Zhang Xian to fetch it in person; aides talked him down and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 帝憂恐不自安，上表申理，方解。

translations.literal: The Emperor worried in fear and was ill at ease; he submitted a memorial clarifying, and only then was it resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan grew fearful and uneasy; a clarifying memorial finally settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 十二月，帝朝於洛陽。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: the Emperor attended court at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Siyuan attended court at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是時，莊宗失政，四方饑饉，軍士匱乏，有賣兒貼婦者，道路怨谘。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong lost proper governance; the four quarters suffered famine; soldiers lacked supplies; some sold children and pawned wives; the roads were full of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu had lost control; famine spread; soldiers went without; some sold children and pawned wives; the roads seethed with complaint.

sentences.zh: 帝在京師，頗為謠言所屬，洎朱友謙、郭崇韜無名被戮，中外大臣皆懷憂懾。

translations.literal: While the Emperor was at the capital he was much pointed to by rumors; when Zhu Youqian and Guo Chongtao were killed without cause, inner and outer great ministers all bore worry and dread.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Siyuan was the target of rumor; when Zhu Youqian and Guo Chongtao were killed without cause, court and command alike were afraid.

sentences.zh: 諸軍馬步都虞候朱守殷奉密旨伺帝起居，守殷陰謂帝曰：「德業振主者身危，功蓋天下者不賞，公可謂振主矣，宜自圖之，無與禍會。

translations.literal: Imperial guard horse and foot overall inspector Zhu Shouyin carried a secret order to watch the Emperor's comings and goings; Shouyin secretly said to the Emperor, "Virtue that shakes the lord endangers the body; merit that covers the realm wins no reward—you may be said to shake the lord; you should plan for yourself and not meet with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial guard inspector Zhu Shouyin was secretly ordered to watch Siyuan; he whispered, "Virtue that outshines the ruler endangers the man; merit that covers the realm goes unrewarded—you shake the throne; plan for yourself before calamity finds you.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾心不負天地，禍福之來，吾無所避，付之於天，卿勿多談也。」

translations.literal: 」The Emperor said, "My heart does not fail heaven and earth; when fortune and calamity come I avoid nothing and leave it to heaven—you need not speak much."
translations.idiomatic: 」Siyuan said, "My heart is clear before heaven and earth; fortune and calamity I do not flee—I leave them to heaven; say no more."

sentences.zh: 四年二月六日，趙在禮據魏州反，莊宗遣元行欽將兵攻之；

translations.literal: Fourth year, second month, sixth day: Zhao Zaili held Ye prefecture in revolt; Zhuangzong sent Yuan Xingqin to lead troops against him;
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the second month in the fourth year Zhao Zaili rebelled at Ye; Cunxu sent Yuan Xingqin against him;

sentences.zh: 行欽不利，退保衛州。

translations.literal: Xingqin was unfavorable and withdrew to guard Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin failed and fell back to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，帝善遇樞密使李紹宏，及帝在洛陽，群小多以飛語謗毀，紹宏每為庇護。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor had treated Privy Council commissioner Li Shaohong well; when the Emperor was at Luoyang, petty men often slandered him with flying words, and Shaohong each time sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan had long favored Li Shaohong of the Privy Council; at Luoyang petty men slandered him, and Shaohong shielded him each time.

sentences.zh: 會行欽兵退，河南尹張全義密奏，請委帝北伐，紹宏讚成之，遂遣帝將兵渡河。

translations.literal: When Xingqin's army withdrew, Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi secretly memorialized asking that the Emperor be entrusted with the northern campaign; Shaohong endorsed it, and the Emperor was then sent to lead troops across the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingqin retreated, Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi secretly urged the northern campaign on Siyuan; Shaohong backed it, and Siyuan was sent across the river.

sentences.zh: 三月六日，帝至鄴都，趙在禮等登城謝罪，出牲餼以勞師，帝亦慰納之，營於鄴城之西南，下令以九日攻城。

translations.literal: Third month, sixth day: the Emperor reached Ye capital; Zhao Zaili and the rest ascended the wall to apologize, sent out oxen and food to comfort the army, and the Emperor also comforted and accepted them; he camped southwest of Ye city and ordered an assault on the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth of the third month Siyuan reached Ye; Zhao Zaili and the rest apologized from the wall and sent food; Siyuan accepted and camped southwest of the city, ordering assault on the ninth.

sentences.zh: 八日夜，軍亂。

translations.literal: On the night of the eighth the army mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the eighth the army mutinied.

sentences.zh: 從馬直軍士有張破敗者，號令諸軍，各殺都將，縱火焚營，歡噪雷動。

translations.literal: Among the horse escort soldiers was Zhang Pobai, who ordered the armies each to kill their commanders, set fires and burn camps, and roared in joy like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: A horse escort named Zhang Pobai ordered each unit to kill its commander, burn the camps, and roar like thunder.

sentences.zh: 至五鼓，亂兵逼帝營，親軍搏戰，傷痍者殆半，亂兵益盛。

translations.literal: By the fifth watch mutinous troops pressed the Emperor's camp; his personal guard fought hand to hand and nearly half were wounded; the mutineers grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth watch mutineers pressed Siyuan's camp; his guard fought until half were down and the rebels still swelled.

sentences.zh: 帝叱之，責其狂逆之狀，亂兵對曰：「昨貝州戍兵，主上不垂厚宥；

translations.literal: The Emperor shouted at them and rebuked their mad rebellion; the mutineers answered, "Yesterday the garrison at Beizhou—Your Majesty showed no generous pardon;
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan shouted and rebuked their treason; they answered, "Yesterday at Beizhou garrison you showed no mercy;

sentences.zh: 又聞鄴城平定之後，欲盡坑全軍。

translations.literal: and after hearing Ye was pacified you intended to bury the whole army alive.
translations.idiomatic: and after Ye fell you meant to slaughter the whole army.

sentences.zh: 某等初無叛誌，直畏死耳。

translations.literal: We had no thought of rebellion at first—we only fear death.
translations.idiomatic: We never meant to rebel—we only fear death.

sentences.zh: 已共諸軍商量，與城中合勢，擊退諸道之師，欲主上帝河南，請令公帝河北。

translations.literal: We have already consulted with the armies and with the city's strength together to beat back the armies of the various circuits; we wish Your Majesty to be emperor south of the river and ask you, sir, to be emperor north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: We have agreed with the garrison to drive off the other columns; we want you emperor south of the river and our lord emperor north.

sentences.zh: 」帝泣而拒之，亂兵呼曰：「令公欲何之？

translations.literal: 」The Emperor wept and refused; the mutineers shouted, "If our lord will not go, where will he go?
translations.idiomatic: 」Siyuan wept and refused; they shouted, "If you will not go north, where will you go?

sentences.zh: 不帝河北，則為他人所有。

translations.literal: If you are not emperor north of the river, you will belong to someone else.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse the north and another will own you.

sentences.zh: 苟不見幾，事當不測！

translations.literal: If you do not see the moment, things will be beyond reckoning!
translations.idiomatic: Miss the moment and anything may happen!

sentences.zh: 」抽戈露刃，環帝左右。

translations.literal: 」They drew swords bare and ringed the Emperor left and right.
translations.idiomatic: 」They bared swords and ringed him.

sentences.zh: 安重誨、霍彥威躡帝足，請詭隨之，因為亂兵迫入鄴城。

translations.literal: An Chonghui and Huo Yanwei trod the Emperor's foot and begged him to follow with deceit; they were thus forced by the mutineers into Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui and Huo Yanwei trod his foot and urged him to pretend consent; mutineers forced him into Ye.

sentences.zh: 懸橋已發，共扶帝越濠而入，趙在禮等歡泣奉迎。

translations.literal: The drawbridge had already been raised; together they helped the Emperor over the moat and in; Zhao Zaili and the rest wept for joy and welcomed him.
translations.idiomatic: The drawbridge was up; they helped him over the moat; Zhao Zaili and the rest wept and welcomed him.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：亂兵擁嗣源及李紹真等入城，城中不受外兵。

translations.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 reads: The mutinous army forced Siyuan and Li Shaozhen and others into the city; within the city they would not receive outside troops.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says mutineers forced Siyuan and Li Shaozhen into the city, which would not admit outside troops.

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉逆擊張破敗，斬之，外兵皆潰。

translations.literal: Huangfu Hui counterattacked Zhang Pobai, beheaded him, and the outside troops all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui struck Zhang Pobai, killed him, and outside troops scattered.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮等率諸校迎拜嗣源。）〉

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili and the rest led the various officers to welcome and bow to Siyuan.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili and the officers welcomed and bowed to Siyuan.)〉

sentences.zh: 是日，饗將士於行宮，在禮等不納外兵，軍眾流散，無所歸向。

translations.literal: That day he feasted the generals and officers at the traveling palace; Zaili and the rest would not admit outside troops, and the army masses drifted away with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: That day he feasted officers at the traveling palace; Zaili barred outside troops and the armies drifted without direction.

sentences.zh: 帝登南樓，謂在禮曰：「欲建大計，非兵不能集事，吾自於城外招撫諸軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended the south tower and said to Zaili, "To establish a great plan troops are needed to gather affairs—I myself will go outside the city to win over the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan climbed the south tower and told Zaili, "A great plan needs troops; I will go outside to rally the armies.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃得出。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor was then able to get out.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was able to leave.

sentences.zh: 夜至魏縣，部下不滿百人。

translations.literal: At night he reached Wei county; his followers numbered fewer than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: By night he reached Wei county with fewer than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 時霍彥威所將鎮州兵五千人獨不亂，聞帝既出，相率歸帝。

translations.literal: At that time the five thousand Zhenzhou troops Huo Yanwei commanded alone did not mutiny; hearing the Emperor had come out, they gathered to him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei's five thousand Zhenzhou men alone held firm; hearing Siyuan was out, they joined him.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，帝登城掩泣曰：「國家患難，一至於此！

translations.literal: At dawn the Emperor ascended the wall, covered his face, and wept, saying, "The state's calamity has come to this!
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he stood on the wall, wept, and said, "The state's trouble has come to this!

sentences.zh: 來日歸藩上章，徐圖再舉。

translations.literal: Tomorrow I shall return to my circuit and submit a memorial, and slowly plan another effort.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow I return to my post and memorialize, then plan again.

sentences.zh: 」安重誨、霍彥威等曰：「此言非便也。

translations.literal: 」An Chonghui, Huo Yanwei, and the rest said, "These words are not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: 」An Chonghui and Huo Yanwei said, "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 國家付以閫外之事，不幸師徒逗撓，為賊驚奔。

translations.literal: The state entrusted you with affairs beyond the passes; unhappily the army faltered and was startled into flight by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The throne entrusted you beyond the passes; the army faltered and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 元行欽狂妄小人，彼在城南，未聞戰聲，無故棄甲；

translations.literal: Yuan Xingqin is a mad petty man; he is south of the city and has not been heard in battle, yet he cast off his armor for no cause;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingqin is a reckless nobody south of the city who never fought yet threw away his armor;

sentences.zh: 如朝天之日，信其奏陳，何所不至！

translations.literal: if on the day you attend court you believe his memorials, what limit would there be!
translations.idiomatic: if you heed his reports at court, what limit is there!

sentences.zh: 若歸藩聽命，便是強據要君，正墮讒慝之口也。

translations.literal: If you return to your circuit and await orders, you would be forcibly holding the ruler to ransom and would fall straight into the mouths of slanderers.
translations.idiomatic: Return to your post and you hold the ruler for ransom and feed the slanderers.

sentences.zh: 正當星行歸闕，面叩玉階，讒間沮謀，庶全功業，無便於此者也。

translations.literal: You should travel like a star back to the capital, face the jade steps, and clear slander and obstruction—only thus may you preserve your achievement; nothing is better than this.
translations.idiomatic: March straight to the capital, face the throne, and clear the slander—only then is your merit safe; nothing better.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor followed them.
translations.idiomatic: 」Siyuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 十一日，發魏縣，至相州，獲官馬二千匹，始得成軍。

translations.literal: On the eleventh he set out from Wei county; reaching Xiangzhou he gained two thousand government horses and only then formed an army.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh he left Wei county; at Xiangzhou he seized two thousand government horses and finally had an army.

sentences.zh: 元行欽退保衛州，果以飛語上奏，帝上章申理，莊宗遣帝子從審及內官白從訓齊詔諭帝。

translations.literal: Yuan Xingqin withdrew to guard Weizhou and indeed submitted flying words; the Emperor submitted a memorial clarifying; Zhuangzong sent the Emperor's son Congshen and inner attendant Bai Congxun together with an edict to instruct the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin held Weizhou and slandered him by memorial; Siyuan answered; Cunxu sent his son Congshen and the eunuch Bai Congxun with an edict.

sentences.zh: 從審至衛州，為行欽所械，帝奏章亦不達。

translations.literal: When Congshen reached Weizhou he was shackled by Xingqin; the Emperor's memorial also did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizhou Xingqin shackled Congshen; Siyuan's memorial never arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝乃趨白皋渡，駐軍於河上，會山東上供綱載絹數船適至，乃取以賞軍，軍士以之增氣。

translations.literal: The Emperor then hurried to Baigao Ford and camped on the river; it happened that several ships of silk tribute from Shandong had just arrived, and he took them to reward the army, and the soldiers' spirit thereby increased.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to Baigao Ford and camped on the river; Shandong tribute silk ships arrived and he paid the troops, lifting their spirits.

sentences.zh: 及將濟，以渡船甚少，帝方憂之。

translations.literal: When they were about to cross, the ferry boats were very few and the Emperor was just then worried.
translations.idiomatic: At the crossing boats were scarce and he worried.

sentences.zh: 忽有木伐數隻，沿流而至，即用以濟師，故無留滯焉。

translations.literal: Suddenly several timber rafts drifted down the current; they were immediately used to ferry the army, and thus there was no delay.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly rafts drifted downriver; they ferried the army without delay.

sentences.zh: 二十六日至汴州，莊宗領兵至滎澤，遣龍驤都校姚彥溫為前鋒。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth he reached Bianzhou; Zhuangzong led troops to Xingze and dispatched Flying Dragon commander Yao Yanwen as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth he reached Bian; Cunxu marched to Xingze and sent Flying Dragon commander Yao Yanwen ahead.

sentences.zh: 是日，彥溫率部下八百騎歸於帝，具言：「主上為行欽所惑，事勢已離，難與共事。

translations.literal: That day Yanwen led his eight hundred cavalry followers to join the Emperor and stated in full, "The ruler is deluded by Xingqin; affairs are already estranged—it is hard to serve together.
translations.idiomatic: That day Yanwen brought eight hundred horse to Siyuan and said, "The ruler trusts Xingqin; the cause is lost—we cannot serve together.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿自不忠，言何悖也！

translations.literal: 」The Emperor said, "You yourself are disloyal—how perverse your words!
translations.idiomatic: 」Siyuan said, "You are the disloyal one—how dare you!

sentences.zh: 」乃奪其兵，仍下令曰：「主上未諒吾心，遂致軍情至此，宜速赴京師。

translations.literal: 」He then seized their troops and still ordered, saying, "The ruler has not yet understood my heart, and thus the army's feeling has come to this—you should hurry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 」He seized their horses and ordered, "The ruler has not understood me and the army is here—hurry to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」既而房知溫、杜晏球自北面相繼而至。

translations.literal: 」Before long Fang Zhiwen and Du Yanqiu arrived in succession from the north face.
translations.idiomatic: 」Soon Fang Zhiwen and Du Yanqiu came up from the north.

sentences.zh: 四月丁亥朔，至罌子穀，聞蕭牆釁作，莊宗晏駕，帝慟哭不自勝。

translations.literal: Fourth month, dinghai new moon: reaching Yingzi Valley he heard trouble within the palace walls; Zhuangzong died suddenly; the Emperor wailed beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai new moon of the fourth month at Yingzi Valley he heard of palace trouble; Cunxu was dead; Siyuan wailed beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，朱守殷遣人馳報：「京城大亂，燔剽不息，請速至京師。

translations.literal: At dawn Zhu Shouyin sent a man galloping to report, "The capital is in great disorder; burning and plundering do not cease—please hurry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Zhu Shouyin sent word, "Luoyang is burning and looting will not stop—come quickly.

sentences.zh: 」己丑，帝至洛陽，止於舊宅，分命諸將止其焚掠。

translations.literal: 」On jichou the Emperor reached Luoyang, halted at his old residence, and in succession ordered the various generals to stop burning and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: 」On jichou he reached Luoyang, stayed at his old house, and ordered the generals to stop the looting.

sentences.zh: 百官弊衣旅見，帝謝之，斂衽泣涕。

translations.literal: The hundred officials came in travel-worn clothes; the Emperor apologized to them, straightened his robe, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Officials came in rags; he apologized, straightened his robe, and wept.

sentences.zh: 時魏王繼岌征蜀未還，帝謂朱守殷曰：「公善巡撫，以待魏王。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Wei Jiji's western campaign against Shu had not yet returned; the Emperor said to Zhu Shouyin, "You are good at patrol and comfort—wait for the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji's Shu campaign had not returned; Siyuan told Zhu Shouyin, "Patrol well and await the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 吾當奉大行梓宮山陵禮畢，即歸藩矣。

translations.literal: I shall follow the late emperor's bier through the mountain tomb rites and then return to my circuit.
translations.idiomatic: I will bury the late emperor and then return to my post.

sentences.zh: 」是日，群臣諸將上箋勸進，帝面諭止之。

translations.literal: 」That day the civil and military ranks and generals submitted memorials urging accession; the Emperor face to face instructed them to stop.
translations.idiomatic: 」That day officials and generals urged him to take the throne; he refused to their faces.

sentences.zh: 樞密使李紹宏、張居翰、宰相豆盧革、韋說、六軍馬步都虞候朱守殷、青州節度使符習、徐州節度使霍彥威、宋州節度使杜晏球、兗州節度使房知溫等頓首言曰：「帝王應運，蓋有天命，三靈所屬，當協冥符。

translations.literal: Privy Council commissioners Li Shaohong and Zhang Juhun, chancellors Dou Luge and Wei Shuo, imperial guard horse and foot overall inspector Zhu Shouyin, Qingzhou military commissioner Fu Xi, Xuzhou military commissioner Huo Yanwei, Songzhou military commissioner Du Yanqiu, Yanzhou military commissioner Fang Zhiwen, and the rest bowed their heads and said, "An emperor's accession surely has heaven's mandate; the three numina belong to him and should accord with the hidden tally.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaohong, Zhang Juhun, Dou Luge, Wei Shuo, Zhu Shouyin, Fu Xi, Huo Yanwei, Du Yanqiu, Fang Zhiwen, and the rest bowed and said, "Heaven chooses the throne; the spirits align; the hidden mandate is his.

sentences.zh: 福之所鍾，不可以謙遜免；

translations.literal: Where fortune is fixed, humility cannot escape it;
translations.idiomatic: Fortune fixed cannot be refused by modesty;

sentences.zh: 道之已喪，不可以智力求。

translations.literal: where the Way is already lost, intellect cannot seek it.
translations.idiomatic: where the Way is lost, wit cannot win it.

sentences.zh: 前代因敗為功，殷憂啟聖，少康重興於有夏，平王再復於宗周，其命維新，不失舊物。

translations.literal: Former ages turned defeat into achievement; deep sorrow opened sage rule—Shaokang revived Xia, Ping Wang restored Zhou; their mandate was renewed without losing the old possession.
translations.idiomatic: Past ages turned defeat to triumph—Shaokang revived Xia, Ping restored Zhou—renewed mandate without losing the realm.

sentences.zh: 今日廟社無依，人神乏主，天命所屬，人何能爭！

translations.literal: Today the temple altars have no reliance and men and spirits lack a lord; heaven's mandate belongs to you—how can men contend!
translations.idiomatic: Today altars stand empty and men and spirits lack a lord; the mandate is yours—who can contest it!

sentences.zh: 光武所謂『使成帝再生，無以讓天下』。

translations.literal: What Guangwu said: "Make Chengdi live again and I could not yield the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As Guangwu said, "Make Chengdi live again and I still could not yield the realm.

sentences.zh: 願殿下俯徇樂推，時哉無失，軍國大事，望以教令施行。

translations.literal: We beg Your Highness to bend to willing push—seize the moment and do not lose it; military and state affairs we hope will be carried out by your teaching orders.
translations.idiomatic: Bend to our push, seize the hour; govern army and state by your command.

sentences.zh: 」帝優答不從。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor answered graciously and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: 」He answered gently and refused.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，文武百僚三拜箋，請行監國之儀，以安宗社，答旨從之。

translations.literal: On renchen the civil and military hundred officials thrice bowed in memorial asking to perform the regency rites to settle the temple altars; he assented.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the hundred officials thrice bowed and asked regency rites to steady the state; he assented.

sentences.zh: 既而有司上監國儀注。

translations.literal: Then the offices submitted regency ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The offices then submitted regency ritual forms.

sentences.zh: 甲午，幸大內興聖宮，始受百僚班見之儀。

translations.literal: On jiawu he visited the inner Great Xingsheng Palace and for the first time received the hundred officials' audience rites.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he entered Great Xingsheng Palace and first received official audience.

sentences.zh: 所司議即位儀注，霍彥威、孔循等言：「唐之運數已衰，不如自創新號。

translations.literal: The offices debated accession ritual regulations; Huo Yanwei, Kong Xun, and the rest said, "Tang's fortune has already declined—it is better to create a new title.
translations.idiomatic: Offices debated enthronement rites; Huo Yanwei and Kong Xun said Tang's fortune was spent and urged a new dynastic name.

sentences.zh: 」因請改國號，不從土德。

translations.literal: They therefore asked to change the state name and did not follow earth virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to change the state name and reject the earth virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝問藩邸侍臣，左右奏曰：「先帝以錫姓宗屬，為唐雪冤，以繼唐祚。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the princely residence attendants; left and right memorialized, saying, "The former emperor because of the granted surname and clan membership avenged Tang and continued Tang's line.
translations.idiomatic: He asked his household staff; they said the late ruler took the Tang surname to avenge Tang and continue its line.

sentences.zh: 今梁朝舊人，不願殿下稱唐，請更名號。

translations.literal: Now men of the old Liang court do not wish Your Highness to be called Tang and ask that the title be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang holdovers do not want you called Tang and ask a new name.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「予年十三事獻祖，以予宗屬，愛幸不異所生。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "At thirteen I served the Founding Ancestor; because I was of his clan he loved and favored me no differently than if born to him.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "At thirteen I served the Founding Ancestor; as his clansman he loved me as a son.

sentences.zh: 事武皇三十年，排難解紛，櫛風沐雨，冒刃血戰，體無完膚，何艱險之不曆！

translations.literal: I served Emperor Wuhuang thirty years, resolved difficulties and ended strife, combed wind and bathed rain, braved blades and fought in blood until my body had no whole skin—what hardship did I not pass!
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years under Wuhuang I fought through wind and rain and blood until no skin was whole—what hardship did I not bear!

sentences.zh: 武皇功業即予功業，先帝天下即予天下也。

translations.literal: Wuhuang's achievement is my achievement; the former emperor's realm is my realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang's merit is mine; the late emperor's realm is mine.

sentences.zh: 兄亡弟紹，於義何嫌。

translations.literal: An elder brother dies and the younger succeeds—what impropriety is there?
translations.idiomatic: Brother dies, younger succeeds—where is the shame?

sentences.zh: 且同宗異號，出何典禮？

translations.literal: Moreover, same clan but a different reign title—what ritual precedent allows this?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, one clan yet a new reign name—what ritual precedent is there for that?

sentences.zh: 曆之衰隆，吾自當之，眾之莠言，吾無取也。

translations.literal: The rise and fall of the dynastic fortune I myself shall bear; the idle talk of the multitude I will not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune's rise and fall are mine to bear; I will not heed the crowd's idle talk.

sentences.zh: 」時群臣集議，依違不定，惟吏部尚書李琪議曰：「殿下宗室勳賢，立大功於三世，一朝雨泣赴難，安定宗社，撫事因心，不失舊物。

translations.literal: 」At this time the assembled ministers deliberated back and forth without deciding; only Minister of Personnel Li Qi argued, saying, "Your Highness is a clansman and meritorious worthy who established great achievement through three reigns; in one morning, weeping in rain you rushed to the crisis, stabilized the altars of state, and governed affairs according to the heart without losing the old inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: 」The ministers debated without settling; only Li Qi of Personnel said, "Your Highness is a clansman and meritorious worthy who served three reigns; weeping you rushed to the crisis, stabilized the altars of state, and governed from the heart without losing the old inheritance.

sentences.zh: 若別新統製，則先朝便是路人，煢煢梓宮，何所歸往！

translations.literal: If you separately create a new system and reign title, then the former court becomes strangers; the lonely imperial coffin—where would it go!
translations.idiomatic: If you create a new system and reign title, the former court becomes strangers—where would the lonely coffin go?

sentences.zh: 不惟殿下追感舊君之義，群臣何安！

translations.literal: Not only would Your Highness fail in the duty of cherishing the former lord's meaning—the ministers, how could they be at ease!
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness would fail to honor the former lord—and how could the ministers be at ease?

sentences.zh: 請以本朝言之，則睿宗、文宗、武宗皆以弟兄相繼，即位柩前，如儲後之儀可也。

translations.literal: I ask, speaking of our own dynasty: Ruizong, Wenzong, and Wuzong all succeeded as brothers, enthroned before the coffin—ceremony like an heir apparent would do.
translations.idiomatic: In our own dynasty Ruizong, Wenzong, and Wuzong all succeeded as brothers before the coffin—heir-apparent ceremony would suffice.

sentences.zh: 」於是群議始定。

translations.literal: 」Thus the assembled debate was finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: 」At that the assembly's debate was settled.

sentences.zh: 河中軍校王舜賢奏，節度使李存霸以今月三日出奔，不知所在。

translations.literal: Hezhong army adjutant Wang Shunxian memorialized that military commissioner Li Cunba fled on the third of this month, whereabouts unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong adjutant Wang Shunxian reported that commissioner Li Cunba fled on the third of this month, whereabouts unknown.

sentences.zh: 乙未，敕曰：「寡人允副群情，方監國事，外安黎庶，內睦宗親，庶諧敦惇之規，永保隆平之運。

translations.literal: On yiwei, an edict said: "I have accepted the people's wish and am overseeing state affairs, securing the people without and harmonizing kinsmen within, hoping to align with honest and sincere norms and ever preserve an age of peace and abundance.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei an edict said, "I have accepted the people's wish and oversee state affairs, securing the people without and harmonizing kin within, hoping for honest governance and lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 昨京師變起，禍難薦臻，至於戚屬之間，不測驚奔之所，慮因藏竄，濫被傷痍，言念於茲，自然流涕。

translations.literal: Yesterday when turmoil rose in the capital and calamity pressed close, even among kin there was no telling where panic flight might lead; fearing that through hiding many would be wrongly harmed, speaking of this my tears naturally flow.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday's capital turmoil brought calamity close; even kin fled in panic to unknown places, and fearing many would be harmed in hiding, I weep at the thought.

sentences.zh: 宜令河南府及諸道，應諸王眷屬等，昨因驚擾出奔，所至之處，即時津送赴闕。

translations.literal: It is proper to order Henan prefecture and all circuits: for princes' dependents who fled yesterday in alarm, wherever they have reached, immediately escort them ferry by ferry to court.
translations.idiomatic: Henan prefecture and all circuits should escort princes' dependents who fled in alarm wherever found straight to court.

sentences.zh: 如不幸物故者，量事收瘞以聞。」

translations.literal: If by misfortune they have died, bury them according to circumstance and report."
translations.idiomatic: If any have died, bury them as circumstances allow and report."

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》：莊宗諸弟存紀、存確匿於南山民家，人有以報安重誨者，重誨曰：「主上以下詔尋訪，帝之仁德，必不加害，不如密令殺之。

translations.literal: (The 《Miscellaneous Dreams of the Northern Realm》 records: Zhuangzong's younger brothers Cunji and Cunque hid in a south-mountain peasant household; someone reported this to An Chonghui, and Chonghui said, "The lord below has issued an edict to seek them; the Emperor's benevolence will surely not harm them—better secretly order them killed.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Miscellaneous Dreams of the Northern Realm》 says Zhuangzong's brothers Cunji and Cunque hid with south-mountain peasants; when someone told An Chonghui, he said, "The throne has ordered a search; the Emperor's grace will not harm them—better have them killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 」果並命於民家。

translations.literal: 」In the end both were put to death in the peasant household.
translations.idiomatic: 」Both were indeed killed in the peasant home.

sentences.zh: 後明宗聞之，切讓重誨，傷惜久之。）〉

translations.literal: Later when Mingzong heard of it he sharply reproached Chonghui and grieved for them a long time.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong later heard, he sharply reproached Chonghui and grieved long.)〉

sentences.zh: 以中門使安重誨為樞密使，以鎮州別駕張延朗為樞密副使，以客將範延光為宣徽使，進奏官馮贇為內客省使。

translations.literal: Central Gate commissioner An Chonghui was made Privy Council commissioner; Zhenzhou vice prefect Zhang Yanlang was made deputy Privy Council commissioner; guest general Fan Yanguang was made Xuanhui commissioner; memorial-presenting officer Feng Yun was made Inner Guest Service commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui of the Central Gate became Privy Council commissioner; Zhang Yanlang, Zhen vice prefect, became deputy commissioner; Fan Yanguang, guest general, became Xuanhui commissioner; Feng Yun, memorial officer, became Inner Guest Service commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丙申，下敕：「今年夏苗，委人戶自供，通頃畝五家為保，本州具帳送省，州縣不得差人檢括。

translations.literal: On bingshen, an edict was issued: "This year's summer field crop tax shall be supplied by households themselves; by mu reckoning, five households form one bao; the prefecture shall compile accounts and send them to the ministry; prefectures and counties may not send men to inspect and seize.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen an edict said, "This summer's field tax shall be reported by households themselves; by mu, five households form one bao; the prefecture shall send accounts to the ministry, and counties may not send inspectors.

sentences.zh: 如人戶隱欺，許人陳告，其田倍征。

translations.literal: If households conceal and cheat, informants are permitted to report; their fields shall be taxed at double."
translations.idiomatic: If households conceal holdings, informants may report them and the land shall be taxed at double."

sentences.zh: 」己亥，命石敬瑭權知陝州兵馬留後，皇子從珂權知河南府兵馬留後。

translations.literal: 」On jihai, Shi Jingtang was ordered to act as acting Shan military commissioner; the prince Congke was ordered to act as acting Henan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: 」On jihai Shi Jingtang was ordered acting Shan commissioner and Prince Congke acting Henan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庚子，淮南楊溥進新茶。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Huainan's Yang Pu presented new tea.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Yang Pu of Huainan presented new tea.

sentences.zh: 以權知汴州軍州事孔循為樞密副使，以陳州刺史劉仲殷為鄧州留後，以鄭州防禦使王思同為同州留後。

translations.literal: Acting Bian military commissioner Kong Xun was made deputy Privy Council commissioner; Chen prefect Liu Zhongyin was made Deng acting commissioner; Zheng defense commissioner Wang Sitong was made Tong acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun, acting Bian commissioner, became deputy Privy Council commissioner; Liu Zhongyin of Chen became Deng acting commissioner; Wang Sitong of Zheng became Tong acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「租庸使孔謙，濫承委寄，專掌重權，侵剝萬端，奸欺百變。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Rent-and-corvée commissioner Kong Qian, having rashly received a heavy commission and monopolized great power, plundered on ten thousand counts and deceived with a hundred shifts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Rent-and-corvée commissioner Kong Qian abused his heavy commission and monopoly power, plundering endlessly and deceiving in every way.

sentences.zh: 遂使生靈塗炭，軍士饑寒，成天下之瘡痍，極人間之疲弊。

translations.literal: He thus made the living smear themselves with ashes and soldiers hunger in cold, making a sore upon All-under-Heaven and exhausting human weariness to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the people to ruin and soldiers to hunger and cold, scourging the realm and exhausting mankind.

sentences.zh: 載詳眾狀，側聽輿辭，難私降黜之文，合正誅夷之典。

translations.literal: Having examined the multitude's accounts and listened to the people's cries, it is hard to grant a private demotion edict—he should receive the proper penalty of execution.
translations.idiomatic: Public accounts and popular outcry make a private demotion impossible—he deserves execution by law.

sentences.zh: 宜削奪在身官爵，按軍令處分。

translations.literal: His personal ranks and titles should be stripped and he punished under military law.
translations.idiomatic: Strip his ranks and punish him under military law.

sentences.zh: 雖犯眾怒，特貸全家，所有田宅，並從籍沒。

translations.literal: Though he offended the multitude's wrath, his whole family is specially spared; all his fields and houses are to be registered and confiscated."
translations.idiomatic: Though the crowd demands his blood, his whole family is spared; all fields and houses are confiscated."

sentences.zh: 」是日，謙伏誅。

translations.literal: 」That day Qian was executed.
translations.idiomatic: 」That day Qian was executed.

sentences.zh: 敕停租庸名額，依舊為鹽鐵、戶部、度支三司，委宰臣豆盧革專判。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the rent-and-corvée title and restored the former Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Expenditure Three Offices, with chief minister Dou Luge placed in sole charge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the rent-and-corvée office and restored the Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Expenditure Three Offices under Dou Luge.

sentences.zh: 中書門下上言：「請停廢諸道鹽運使、內勾司、租庸院大程官，出放豬羊柴炭戶。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: "We ask to abolish circuit salt transport commissioners, inner auditing offices, rent-and-corvée bureau senior clerks, and the releasing of pig, sheep, firewood, and charcoal households.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat memorialized, "Abolish circuit salt transport commissioners, inner auditing offices, rent-and-corvée bureau senior clerks, and pig, sheep, firewood, and charcoal household releases.

sentences.zh: 括田竿尺，一依朱梁制度，仍委節度、刺史通申三司，不得差使量檢。

translations.literal: Land survey rods and rules shall follow the Former Liang system entirely; still entrust circuit commissioners and prefects to report jointly to the Three Offices, and they may not send agents to measure and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Land surveys shall follow Former Liang rules; commissioners and prefects shall report to the Three Offices without sending measuring agents.

sentences.zh: 州使公廨錢物，先被租庸院管係，今據數卻還州府，州府不得科率百姓。

translations.literal: Prefectural public funds previously held by the rent-and-corvée bureau are now returned to prefectures in counted amounts; prefectures may not levy the people.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural funds held by the rent-and-corvée bureau are returned in full; prefectures may not levy the people.

sentences.zh: 百姓合散蠶鹽，每年隻二月內一度亻表散，依夏稅限納錢。

translations.literal: The people's combined silkworm salt distribution shall be allotted only once a year within the second month, with payment due by the summer-tax deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Combined silkworm salt for the people shall be allotted only once yearly in the second month, payable by the summer-tax deadline.

sentences.zh: 夏秋苗稅子，除元征石鬥及地頭錢，餘外不得紐配。

translations.literal: Summer and autumn field taxes, apart from the originally levied grain per dou and the ground-head money, may have no further surcharges.
translations.idiomatic: Summer and autumn field taxes may add nothing beyond the original grain levy per dou and ground-head money.

sentences.zh: 先遇赦所放逋稅，租庸違制征收，並與除放。

translations.literal: Arrears remitted by prior amnesties but collected in violation of rent-and-corvée rules shall also be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears amnestied earlier but illegally collected under rent-and-corvée rules are also remitted.

sentences.zh: 今欲曉告河南府及諸道準此施行。

translations.literal: We now wish to proclaim this to Henan prefecture and all circuits for implementation."
translations.idiomatic: We ask to proclaim this to Henan and all circuits for implementation."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: 」The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 是日，宋州節度使元行欽伏誅。

translations.literal: That day Song military commissioner Yuan Xingqin was executed.
translations.idiomatic: That day Yuan Xingqin, Song commissioner, was executed.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以樞密副使孔循為樞密使。

translations.literal: On renyin, deputy Privy Council commissioner Kong Xun was made Privy Council commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Kong Xun became Privy Council commissioner.
